Deprecation.description: RFC 9745: the route or a field of the request is deprecated (since the date given, `@<unix seconds>`). Routes also send `Link: <successor>; rel="successor-version"`.

ConfirmDelete.description:
Guard against deleting the wrong resource: the ID or the exact name of
the sandbox or snapshot being deleted. When sent, any other value
(empty, another resource's name or ID, or the header twice) is
`409 delete_confirmation_required` and nothing is deleted; the
Idempotency-Key can then be reused. A sandbox delete with an API key
created on or after the server's `confirmDeleteKeysFrom` cutover must
send it (without it: the same 409, naming the ID to send); otherwise,
without the header, the delete proceeds as before (an API key's
response then carries a `Warning` header). The instabox CLI, the SDKs,
the hosted MCP server and the dashboard send it.
ConfirmDelete.name: X-Confirm-Delete

IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-generated key, 1-200 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the
user. Same key and same method+path+body returns the original response;
same key with a different request returns `409 idempotency_conflict`.
Records are kept for 7 days.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

MachineRef.description: Sandbox ID (`m_` + 26 lowercase base32 characters) or the sandbox's name (unique among your sandboxes; names never contain `_`, so the two never collide). Older servers take only the ID and answer `404` for a name.
MachineRef.name: id

SnapshotID.description: Snapshot ID (`sn_`, or `im_` for older snapshots, + 26 lowercase base32 characters).
SnapshotID.name: id

BadRequest.description: `bad_request`: invalid input or missing Idempotency-Key. `unknown_field`: a body key that is no field of the request's schema (create, fork, restore, start, stop, suspend, resume, wake and `PATCH` of a sandbox); the message names it and the closest known field (`did you mean "templateId"?`) and lists the known ones. Nothing is changed. `spec_not_allowed`: sandbox sizes are fixed (4 vCPUs, 8 GiB memory by default; `limits.machineSpec`) and the request names another size (create, create from a snapshot), or someone other than an admin tries to grow the disk of a free sandbox or of a sandbox whose owner may not resize disks. On `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}` it is also a `vcpus`/`memMiB` size the workspace's plan does not offer (the message lists the plan's sizes) or any new size for a free sandbox, whose size is fixed. The message gives the size the sandbox gets; leaving the size fields out always works. `invalid_guest_user`: a create's `guestUser` is not a valid Linux user name or is reserved (`root`, `instabox`, the Debian base system's users and groups such as `sudo`, `systemd-*`). `vault_unavailable` (503): a Vault item was sealed under a master key this server does not have (docs/vault.md).

Conflict.description:
`operation_conflict` (another operation is active; `operationId` names it,
or the transition is not allowed), `idempotency_conflict` (key reused for
a different request), `delete_confirmation_required` (a delete's
`X-Confirm-Delete` header is not the sandbox's or snapshot's ID or name,
or a key that must send it left it out),
`machine_not_running` (the sandbox is not running), `desktop_not_running` (the
VNC endpoint before the desktop started), or for Orca connections
`orca_unsupported` and `runtime_not_ready` (retryable).

MetricsUnavailable.description: `metrics_unavailable`: the metrics store is turned off (`metrics.storeUrl` "off"), not running or failing. Retryable when it is down.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: no such resource (also for deleted sandboxes).

OperationAccepted.description: The mutation was accepted (or replayed for the same idempotency key). Poll the operation.

PaymentRequired.description: `credit_exhausted`: the account's free sandbox used its hours for the month (when the server enforces a cap); it can run again next month (UTC). `spend_limit_reached`: the sandbox's paid org reached its spend cap for the month. `subscription_required`: the org's subscription ended. `payment_failed`: the charge a plan change needed did not succeed; the plan is unchanged.

PermissionDenied.description: `permission_denied`: the user is not allowed (not on the allowlist, or not the owner), or an API key was used where only a sign-in session is; `missing_scope`: the API key lacks the route's scope (`requiredScopes` names it; older servers sent `insufficient_scope`).

QuotaExceeded.description: `quota_exceeded`: one of your limits was reached: the number of sandboxes (on the free plan 1, in any state, stopped and paused included; Pro 500; Builder 1000), stored data (on the free plan 200 GiB), snapshots (on the free plan 5), API keys, execs or terminals. The message says which, e.g. "sandbox limit reached (1 of 1) in org alice (free plan): delete a sandbox first". Delete a sandbox or snapshot, upgrade the plan, or ask an admin to raise your limit.

Unauthenticated.description: A credential 401 has its own code: `missing_key`, `malformed_key`, `invalid_key`, `expired_key`, `revoked_key` or `session_expired`, with `hint` and `docs` (older servers sent `unauthenticated`, `api_key_expired` or `api_key_revoked`). Other 401s (refresh tokens, tickets) are `unauthenticated`. For a missing or bad API key or access token the message ends with how to get a key (session and refresh-token 401s say to sign in again instead), e.g. `create an API key at https://dashboard.instabox.sh/dashboard/api-keys and send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>" or "X-API-Key: <key>"`.

Unavailable.description: `no_capacity` (there is no room for the sandbox right now; the message says what could not run and when to retry) or `host_unavailable` (the sandbox cannot be reached right now). Usually `retryable`; try again shortly. `no_capacity` is `retryable`: retry with exponential backoff (for example after 15 s, 30 s, 60 s, then every few minutes), or try another size or template. A create whose operation failed with it replays that failed operation for the same `Idempotency-Key`, so retry it with a new key. With `--fail-fast` the CLI's `create` and `run` exit 75 on it (otherwise 1). A retryable `no_capacity` has `retryAfterSeconds` and the same `Retry-After` header: wait at least that long before the first retry.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying; the body's `retryAfterSeconds`.

lastUsedAt.description: Updated at most once a minute.

prefix.description: First 8 characters after `ibk_`, for recognizing the key.

version.description: The dashboard's version of the rules it showed.

admin.description: The account is an administrator now (an admin code grants the role).

email.description: Who the agent expects to claim, if it said.

expiresAt.description: Until when the code can be claimed.

expiresInDays.description: The key life asked for; 0: never expires.

code.description: The user code the agent printed (`XXXX-XXXX`).

expiresInDays.description: Shortens the requested expiry; a finite request cannot be lengthened or made `0` (never), which is `400`.

scopes.description: Grants only these of the scopes the agent asked for: a non-empty subset of them (a scope it did not ask for is `400`).

userId.description: Optional: must be the session's account.

state.description: `claimed`: the agent's next poll gets its key.

key.description: The secret, shown only in this reply and to polls repeated within the 10-minute delivery window.

userId.description: The account the key belongs to.

email.description: Who is expected to claim, shown to them as a hint. Nothing is sent to it.

expiresInDays.description: The key's requested life in days, 1-365. 0 or absent: a key that does not expire. The person may shorten it.

name.description: The key's name, shown to the person who claims and on the API keys page (default `agent`).

scopes.description: Default `machines:read machines:write machines:delete images:read`. The person may approve fewer.

claimToken.description: `ibg_...`, the agent's secret for `POST /v1/auth/agent/token`. Shown to no one.

expiresIn.description: Seconds the code can be claimed for.

name.description: The key's name, after the default.

scopes.description: The scopes asked for, after the default.

userCode.description: What the person enters on the claim page, `XXXX-XXXX`.

verificationUriComplete.description: The claim page with the code filled in. Show the code anyway.

ack.description: Acknowledge the delivered key once it is stored; the server erases its sealed copy and later polls answer `expired_token`.

AutoSuspendAfterSeconds.description: Absent: 1800 (30 minutes). The plan decides, and a value is honoured or refused, never silently replaced: a paid sandbox takes 300-1800 (5 to 30 minutes) in whole minutes, as sent, and 0 (off) where the plan allows always on (else `403 spec_not_allowed`); below 300 (1-299), above 1800, negative or not a multiple of 60 is `400 bad_request`. The free sandbox is fixed at 1800: any other value is `403 spec_not_allowed`, a plan limit (older servers: `403 permission_denied`). A refused create makes no sandbox. The reply's `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` shows the effective value. Separately, an account an admin gave manual lifecycle (`GET /v1/me` `manualLifecycle`) sends 120-86400 idle seconds, or 0 never (docs/idle-suspend.md).

code.description: One-time code (`ibc_...`) from the redirect URI.

tier.description: The tier to subscribe to; absent: a disabled workspace's own, or on a free workspace a card to save.

org.description: The org; absent when the Checkout buys a new workspace.

url.description: The Stripe Checkout URL to send the user to; empty when the org is on the plan already (its credits covered the rest of the month, or the card on file paid).

id.description: Connection ID (`cn_…`), also the certificate key ID.

capabilities.description: `mosh`: mosh works (a session that runs `mosh-server new` gets a relay UDP port in its `MOSH CONNECT` line).

moshHost.description: Optional separate Mosh gateway host; defaults to host when absent.

moshPort.description: SSH port for Mosh session bootstrap; defaults to port when absent. The UDP relay port is negotiated during bootstrap.

expiresInDays.description: Days until the key expires, 1-365. 0 or absent: it does not expire.

publicKey.description: Client public key in authorized_keys format.

CreateMachineRequest.description: Every field is optional; a body key that is none of these is refused with `400 unknown_field` (keys match case-insensitively). The lifetime timeout retired on 2026-10-20 is refused too; `timeoutSeconds`, `onTimeout` or `timeout` with any value but null is `400 unknown_field`, and the message names `deleteAfterSeconds`, `maxRunMinutes` and `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` instead (to a `User-Agent` of `instabox-cli/<version>`, whose builds before that date sent them, it says the CLI is out of date, how to install the current one, and names the flags `--delete-after`, `--max-run-minutes` and `--auto-suspend`). At most one of `templateId` and `snapshotId`; with neither, the sandbox starts from agent-browser, the CLI's and dashboard's default. Leave the size fields out for the default size, or name the `vcpus` and `memMiB` of another of your sizes (the org's plan's or one an admin granted the org; `GET /v1/orgs` `allowedSpecs`).

archiveSeconds.description: Sets `archiveAt` to now plus this many seconds: the sandbox is stopped then if it is running. 0 or absent: none.

deleteAfterSeconds.description: Sets `deleteAt` to now plus this many seconds (60-86400, else 400): the sandbox is then deleted, whatever its state, so it cannot outlive a client that died (`instabox run` sets it). 0 or absent: never. A server without this field ignores it.

directSecrets.description: Direct (delivery env) Secrets from this org, each as a variable and/or a home file. Real values enter the sandbox; prefer proxy Secrets for HTTPS API keys. A fork that sends none of secrets, envSecrets and directSecrets copies its source's selection.

env.description: Environment variables for the whole sandbox: every login shell exports them (exec, SSH, the terminal and what they start), from the first command on and again after each start and resume. Names match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$`; `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `HOME`, `HOSTNAME`, `IFS`, `LOGNAME`, `OLDPWD`, `PATH`, `PWD`, `SHELL`, `SHLVL`, `USER`, bash's readonly `BASHOPTS`, `BASH_VERSINFO`, `EUID`, `PPID`, `SHELLOPTS` and `UID`, the session's `TERM`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, the trust roots `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, and names starting `INSTABOX_` or `SSH_` are reserved (set them per exec); values have no NUL bytes; names and values at most 32 KiB together. Not on Windows templates (400). On macOS, bash and zsh login shells export them, and zsh's special parameters (`status`, `path`, `options`, `HISTSIZE`, `USERNAME`, ...) and `ZDOTDIR` are reserved too. Fixed at create: a fork takes its source's, a create from a snapshot only its own. An exec's `envs`, a Vault item and an env Secret of the same name win. Not Secrets: anything in the sandbox can read the values, and the sandbox shows only the names (`envNames`). The values are stored encrypted at rest; a site without the Secret master key refuses env (400 bad_request).

envSecrets.description: Explicit env Secret names from this org; omitted or [] selects none. No all mode; null is rejected. Real values enter the sandbox. Shorthand for directSecrets entries with env = the Secret's name; not sent together with directSecrets.

failFast.description: When no host has room for the sandbox right now, refuse the create at once with `503 no_capacity` (`retryable`; nothing is created, there is no operation and the `Idempotency-Key` is not kept) instead of answering 202 with an operation that then fails with `no_capacity`. Every other check and the rest of the create are unchanged; a host that had room can still fill up before the operation places the sandbox. The check does not ask for a host with the secret proxy, which a create with `secrets` or `envSecrets` needs: if only hosts without it have room, the create is accepted and its operation fails with `no_capacity`. A create from a snapshot that no host can start now is refused too, instead of being created stopped. A server without this field ignores it, or, if it already refuses unknown body keys, answers `400 unknown_field`.

gpu.description: GPUs for the sandbox: `TYPE` (one GPU) or `TYPE:COUNT`, such as `l4` or `l4:2`, a type of the GPU template's `gpuTypes` (`GET /v1/templates`). GPU sandboxes are for paid plans: a free org's create is `403 template_not_allowed`. The count is at most the type's `maxPerMachine`, and an org's sandboxes have at most 8 GPUs in all (`403 template_limit` past it; a stopped sandbox keeps its GPUs counted). The template defaults to `gpu`, and the size comes from the type: one of its `sizes`, per GPU (`l4:2` gets twice the vCPUs and memory, the same disk; `vcpus` and `memMiB` pick another of its sizes, multiplied). An unknown type, a template without GPU support or a count over the limit is `400 bad_request`; with `snapshotId`, only the GPU of the snapshot's sandbox. GPUs are billed per GPU-hour while the sandbox runs, on top of its vCPUs and memory. Absent: no GPU.

guestUser.description: The sandbox's Linux user (`Machine.guestUser`), so `ssh <sandbox>` over your own network (Tailscale) logs in as the same name as on your computer. Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters; reserved names (`root`, `instabox`, the Debian base system's users and groups such as `sudo`, `systemd-*`) are refused with `400 invalid_guest_user`. Clients send the local username normalized (`DOMAIN\alice` and `alice@corp.example` become `alice`, lowercase, spaces become `_`) and nothing when that is not a valid name. Absent: `user`; with `snapshotId`, the snapshot's user. Ignored (the sandbox gets `dev`) for templates without the `guest-user` capability. Fixed at create.

imageId.description: Deprecated: `snapshotId` under its old name (both: they must be equal). The reply carries a `Deprecation` header.

memMiB.description: Like vcpus: the memory (MiB) of one of your sizes, such as 8192 with vcpus 4; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`.

name.description: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, starting with a letter or digit; unique among the org's sandboxes. Absent or empty: `box-` and 8 random hex digits (the operation's `machineId` and the sandbox carry it).

orgId.description: The org the sandbox counts against and is shared with (`GET /v1/orgs`); you must be a member. Absent: your personal org, or with `snapshotId` the snapshot's org (a sandbox from a snapshot lives in the snapshot's org; another is `400 bad_request`). Secret selections always resolve within this org. The org's sandbox limit and, on the free tier, its monthly included usage apply (`429 quota_exceeded`, `402 credit_exhausted`).

persistentDiskGiB.description: Storage (`/data`) size in GiB. The disks come with the size: storage gets the size's (20 GiB on api.instabox.sh), or a snapshot's storage size when that is larger. Absent or exactly that size: accepted; any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` whose message names the size's storage next to what was asked; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`. To get more storage, grow it later with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`: a running sandbox's storage grows live, and a shrink applies while it is stopped, at its next boot. The SDKs' `diskGiB` (TypeScript) and `persistent_disk_gib` (Python) are this field; `diskGiB` in a REST body is `400 unknown_field`.

pool.description: Admins only: the host pool to place the sandbox in and no other (docs/hybrid-pools.md), "default" included. With snapshotId it must be the snapshot's pool. Absent: the user's pool assignment, else the server's placement.createPools.

rootDiskGiB.description: System files size in GiB. Like persistentDiskGiB: system files get the template's size (or the snapshot's); naming any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` (the message names the size's root disk), 0 or a negative `400 bad_request`; grow it later with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`.

secrets.description: Proxy Secrets from this org. All includes current and future proxy Secrets; [] selects none. Omit both secrets and envSecrets to retain only existing Vault delivery. When envSecrets alone is supplied, proxy selection defaults to all; directSecrets alone selects no proxy Secrets. Null is rejected.

snapshotId.description: Create from this snapshot of yours: its system files and storage (empty storage for a system-files-only snapshot).

templateId.description: The template to create from (`GET /v1/templates`, one with `creatable` true), optionally with a version as `id@version` (e.g. `agent-browser@2026-10-15.4`, the same as `templateVersion`). Absent (and no `snapshotId` or `templateVersion`): agent-browser. An unknown or retired one is refused with `400 bad_request` whose message lists the templates your plan can create from. The free plan creates from agent-browser, android, omarchy or ci only; another template is refused with `403 template_not_allowed`. A create from a snapshot is not limited.

templateVersion.description: Default: the version `GET /v1/templates` marks `latest`. `templateId` may name it instead, as `id@version` (e.g. `agent-browser@2026-10-15.4`); both at once must agree. A version the template does not have is `400 bad_request` whose message lists its versions, newest first, the `latest` (or `default`) one tagged.

vault.description: False disables legacy Vault delivery. Org Secret selections are independent.

vcpus.description: Absent: the default size (4 vCPUs, 8 GiB memory; `limits.machineSpec`). Else one of the org's sizes (`GET /v1/orgs` `allowedSpecs`: the default, its plan's others and any size an admin granted the org; on api.instabox.sh free 4/8192 only, Pro 2/4096, 4/8192, 8/16384, Builder 2/4096 up to 16/32768, Team and Enterprise 2/4096 up to 32/65536), or, from a template with a `pool` (macOS, Windows), its `defaultSpec` or one of its `sizes`, whatever the plan; name memMiB too when two of them have this many vCPUs. Anything else is refused with `400 spec_not_allowed`; 0 or a negative (no size) with `400 bad_request`.

scope.description: Orca device scope of the assertion: `runtime` (default, full access) or `mobile` (Orca's mobile method allowlist, push registration).

email.description: Whom to invite; only an account with this email can join with it.

role.description: The role the invitee joins with (default member).

name.description: Optional display name; whitespace is trimmed, at most 100 UTF-8 bytes. Existing callers may omit it.

noExpiry.description: A token that works until it is revoked: the reply has no `expiresAt`. Does not go with `ttlSeconds`.

forFork.description: Saved to fork its source (`instabox fork`, when the native fork cannot run). For a free source, the server records its max-run window as activity extended it, and a sandbox the same user creates from this snapshot in the next 30 minutes starts with that window, as a native fork does. Names no window.

name.description: Unique among the caller's snapshots; 1-63 of a-z, 0-9, '-', starting with a letter or digit.

rootOnly.description: Save the system files only, not the storage (`/data`).

mode.description: Octal permissions, for example 0755 (default an existing file's, else 0644).

path.description: Absolute path of the file to write.

expiresInDays.description: Days until the key expires, 1-365. 0 or absent: it does not expire.

scopes.description: `APIKeyScope`s, or in a workspace `workspace:admin` (also what absent means there). A personal org's key needs some.

key.description: The secret, shown only in this reply and to polls repeated within the 10-minute delivery window.

name.description: The workspace's name, exactly: the confirmation.

DeprecatedImage.description: A snapshot as the deprecated /v1/images routes return it.

actions.description: The computer-use MCP's last tool calls (at most 20, oldest first), as its proxy logged them.

agentPausable.description: The sandbox's computer-use MCP honors the control (its wrapper runs the server through the proxy). False on a sandbox made before the proxy existed: a takeover would not pause its agent, so clients should offer watching only.

controlError.description: The control file in the sandbox could not be written (its runtime directory is missing or not writable): takeover and handback cannot take effect. The reason, from the sandbox.

controller.description: Who drives the desktop: `agent` (the default; viewers watch) or `human` (a viewer took over, and the computer-use MCP refuses input until they hand back or 30 s pass without a call from them).

failed.description: The last install failed; log holds its last lines.

hint.description: Only on a `start` that started nothing because the desktop is not installed (`start` never installs), is still installing, or failed to install: what to send next. Absent otherwise.

kind.description: The desktop the sandbox has. `vm` (a Windows or Mac sandbox): its VM's own screen, always running and controlled by every viewer (`controller` `human`, `yours`); `install`, `start`, `takeover` and `handback` change nothing. `x11` (absent from servers before this field): Xvnc and Xfce, installed on first use, driven by the computer-use MCP. `wayland` (the omarchy template): a compositor that starts at boot and is in the image: `install` changes nothing, `start` only brings the session and its VNC server up and sizes the display, and there is no computer-use MCP (`agentPausable` is false); watch and use it through VNC.

running.description: The VNC server answers: GET /v1/machines/{id}/vnc connects.

yours.description: The caller (its sign-in session or API key) is the viewer in control. Absent when false.

args.description: Its arguments, strings shortened to 80 characters.

refused.description: Refused because a human controlled the desktop; it never reached the tool.

tool.description: The MCP tool called (click, type_text, get_app_state, ...).

height.description: Screen height in pixels for start, 600-1600 (default 800).

width.description: Screen width in pixels for start, 800-2560 (default 1280).

url.description: The dashboard's full-screen viewer, `<dashboard>/desktop/{id}#token=...`; open it or embed it in an iframe.

ttlSeconds.description: How long the link opens the desktop.

viewOnly.description: The link only shows the desktop; the server drops the viewer's input.

provider.description: The device sign-in the flow uses: `github` (GitHub's device flow) or `workos` (WorkOS CLI Auth, GitHub or Google). Absent from servers before it.

verificationUriComplete.description: `verificationUri` with the user code filled in, when the device sign-in offers one (WorkOS's does, GitHub's does not). Clients open it and still show the code to compare.

invite.description: An invite code (`K7R2QX`; older `482913` and `ibi_...` codes work too) for an account that is not activated yet; spaces around it, spaces or dashes inside a 6-character code and case do not matter.

provider.description: Optional. Absent or `github`: the server's default device sign-in. `workos`: WorkOS's, wherever WorkOS is configured (docs/workos.md), else `400`. `google`: WorkOS's where WorkOS is the default, else `400` (its dark launch admits administrators only). Servers before it ignore the field, so a client asking for `google` or `workos` checks the reply's `provider` is `workos` before showing the code.

DirectSecret.description: A reference to a direct (delivery env) Secret: its real value as the variable `env` (exported by login shells), as a file at `file` (home-relative; the value stays on tmpfs at /run/instabox/secrets/files and the home path is a symlink to it), or both. Names and paths only; values are never returned.

env.description: Not reserved (PATH, HOME, BASH_ENV, IFS, CA variables, ...) and no INSTABOX_ or SSH_ prefix.

file.description: Clean path relative to the home directory, without .. components.

username.description: The Discord username when it was linked.

link.description: The linked Discord account; null when none is linked.

message.description: What is full and how to free or add space (delete files, `instabox resize <box> --disk N` for /data: a running sandbox's disk grows live).

mount.description: The fullest filesystem (empty when it could not be read after a command ran out of space).

noSpace.description: The command failed with No space left on device (or Disk quota exceeded).

at.description: When it happened, for a stop the platform found (a sandbox's `lastError` with code `host_oom`, `vmm_crashed` or `guest_reboot_loop`; `hint` says what to do). The next successful start clears the error. Absent otherwise and from older servers.

code.description: Machine-readable code. HTTP status per code is fixed.

docs.description: A URL documenting the error (credential errors). Absent otherwise.

docs_url.description: The code's entry on the errors page, on every error response: https://instabox.sh/docs/errors#<code> with underscores as dashes (e.g. #credit-exhausted): its HTTP status, whether to retry and what to do. Snake case, unlike the other fields. Absent from a failed operation's `error` and from older servers.

hint.description: The next step that fixes the error (credential errors). Absent otherwise.

reason.description: The same as `code` for credential errors (401 `missing_key`, `malformed_key`, `invalid_key`, `expired_key`, `revoked_key`, `session_expired`; 403 `missing_scope`). For 409 `machine_cooldown`, the automatic abuse check whose pause locks the sandbox: `abuse_egress_blocklist` (it tried to connect to a blocked destination on the egress blocklist, not a DNS lookup), `abuse_network_flows` (scanning or attack traffic), `abuse_cpu` (mining); absent for a max-run cooldown. For a retryable 409 `fork_unavailable`, why the source's host cannot take the fork: `source_host_unavailable` (it takes no new sandboxes) or `source_host_full` (no room now). Absent on other errors and from older servers.

requiredScopes.description: For `missing_scope`, the scopes the route accepts; the key needs one of them.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Seconds to wait before trying again: a retryable `no_capacity` (60, as a 503 or on a failed operation's `error`), `rate_limited`, `machine_cooldown` and agent sign-up `quota_exceeded`. An error response also sends it as the `Retry-After` header; a failed operation's `error` has only this field. Absent otherwise and from older servers.

retryable.description: True if the same request may succeed later.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` of the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

ExecHistoryEntry.description: One command of a sandbox's history: an exec request that reached the sandbox, whoever sent it, as the server recorded it. `stdout` and `stderr` are set only by `GET /v1/machines/{id}/history/{execId}`.

command.description: The request's `cmd`, its `argv` quoted for a shell, or its `historyCommand`; cut at 4096 bytes.

outputTruncated.description: The stored output is cut: the history keeps the first 64 KiB of each stream.

signal.description: The signal that killed the command, as the sandbox named it (absent otherwise).

status.description: How the command ended: `exited` (exit code reported; `signal` set if a signal killed it), `timed_out` (killed after `timeoutSeconds`), `lost` (the connection to the sandbox ended before the exit status; it may have run), `cancelled` (the client closed the request; the command was killed) or `unreachable` (the sandbox could not be reached; nothing ran).

streamed.description: The client streamed the output (`Accept: text/event-stream`).

truncated.description: The exec's result had its output cut at 1 MiB per stream (never for a streamed exec).

ExecRequest.description: Set exactly one of `cmd` (a shell string) and `argv` (a program and its arguments, run without a shell); both, neither or an empty `argv` is `400 bad_request`. An empty `cmd` counts as no `cmd`, so `{"cmd": "", "argv": [...]}` runs the `argv`.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, run with no shell: each element reaches the program exactly as sent (no expansion of `$`, `*` or `~`, no word splitting, quotes or redirections; `""` is an empty argument). `argv[0]` must not be empty and is looked up on the login profile's `PATH`; the login profile, `envs` and `cwd` apply as for `cmd`. A program that is not found exits 127, one that cannot run 126. At most 64 KiB counting each element's length plus one, no NUL bytes. The command sent to the sandbox (`envs`, `cwd` and `argv`, quoted for the shell: about 9 bytes per element plus its text) must also stay under 128 KiB, so many short elements can be `400 bad_request` below the 64 KiB cap; send bulk data on `stdin`. Set this or `cmd`.

cmd.description: Shell command, run with `bash -lc`. At most 64 KiB, no NUL bytes. Set this or `argv`; an empty `cmd` is no `cmd`.

envs.description: Environment variables exported before the command (after the login profile). Names match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`.

historyCommand.description: How the command appears in the sandbox's history instead of `cmd` or `argv`, for a wrapper that runs something else (the CLI's `exec --background`). Cut at 4096 bytes like them; no NUL bytes.

noHistory.description: Leave the command out of the sandbox's history (`GET /v1/machines/{id}/history`): for a client's own housekeeping commands, such as the CLI's job polls. Does not go with `historyCommand`.

secretEnvs.description: Direct (delivery env) Secrets of the sandbox's org exported for this command only: variable name -> Secret name. Resolved at exec time, never stored or written into the sandbox; each use is audited by name. A name may not also be in `envs`; reserved variables are refused. A proxy or missing Secret is 400. Only where `GET /v1/me` has `directSecretRefs`; elsewhere 400 (a control host from before secretEnvs would run the command without them).

stdin.description: Text fed to the command, then EOF. It is a JSON string, so the command reads its UTF-8 bytes: NUL, CR and LF arrive unchanged (escaped as `\u0000`, `\r`, `\n`). At most 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) of UTF-8, counted in bytes, not characters (`é` is 2): more is `400 bad_request` `stdin is longer than 1048576 bytes`. The schema sets no `maxLength` here, because `maxLength` counts characters. JSON cannot carry bytes that are not UTF-8; any in the request body reach the command as U+FFFD (`ef bf bd`), with no error. For binary input, send it base64-encoded and decode it in the command (`base64 -d | ...`; up to 768 KiB of binary fits), or write the file first with `PUT /v1/machines/{id}/files` and redirect it in (`cmd < file`). The CLI's `exec --stdin` does that upload itself for input past 1 MiB or not UTF-8, up to 5 GiB.

diskWarning.description: Set when the command failed with No space left on device (read again right after it), or a filesystem was at least 90% full when last read (read in the background after an exec or metrics call, at most once a minute).

exitCode.description: Exit status; 128+N if killed by standard signal N, otherwise 255 with `signal` set; 124 if timed out.

invalidUtf8.description: stdout or stderr had bytes that are not UTF-8 (binary output), replaced with U+FFFD, so the output is not what the command wrote. Absent when false; also set on a streamed exec's exit event.

oomKill.description: The OOM kill behind `oomKilled` (the newest, when several).

oomKilled.description: The command exited non-zero and the sandbox's kernel OOM killer killed one of its own processes (the command or a child: its SSH session's cgroup; never another command's process, and each kill is reported once). `oomKill` says which, when the sandbox named it. Checked only for exit code 137, a signal, or stderr saying a process was killed. False when none was seen, the exec's session scope could not be read, or the sandbox's host or guest agent cannot report kills; a kill whose kernel log record was lost is still true when the session scope's oom_kill count shows it (`oomKill` absent). Absent from older servers. Also set on a streamed exec's exit event.

signal.description: The signal that killed the command, as the sandbox named it (absent otherwise).

timedOut.description: The command ran past `timeoutSeconds` and was killed.

truncated.description: stdout or stderr was longer than 1 MiB and was cut.

Export.description: A `.tar.gz` of a sandbox's or a snapshot's `/data` disk (home and workspace), built from the disk's saved copy while its workspace is paused or disabled. Exactly one of `machineId` and `snapshotId` is set.

expiresAt.description: When a ready archive is deleted, 7 days after it was built and never after the workspace's data.

name.description: The sandbox's or snapshot's name when the export was asked for.

savedAt.description: When the disk was saved: the sandbox's last stop or pause, or the snapshot.

sha256.description: The archive's SHA-256 (hex), once ready; also its download ETag.

status.description: `ready`: download it. `failed`: `error` says why; ask again. `expired`: deleted; ask again while the workspace is paused or disabled.

exportable.description: True while the workspace is paused for a failed payment or disabled: exports can be asked for.

purgeAt.description: When the workspace's sandboxes and snapshots are deleted.

sources.description: The sandboxes and snapshots the caller may export, each with its newest export that has not expired.

target.description: A symbolic link's target, as stored.

created.description: The file is new (201); false when it replaced one (200).

path.description: The file written, with symbolic links resolved.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the bytes the server received and wrote.

binary.description: The file is not UTF-8 text; content is empty.

entries.description: A directory's entries, directories first, then by name.

path.description: The path read, with symbolic links resolved.

truncated.description: The directory has more entries, or the file more bytes, than returned.

autoSuspendAfterSeconds.description: As in CreateMachineRequest. Absent: the source's (0, off, when it has none), checked against the plan as a create's.

deleteAfterSeconds.description: As in CreateMachineRequest (60-86400). Absent or 0: the source's delete deadline, the same instant (none if the source has none); a source due within 60 seconds is then refused with 400.

directSecrets.description: As in CreateMachineRequest; alone, it selects no proxy Secrets.

maxRunMinutes.description: As in CreateMachineRequest. Absent: the source's (the plan default when it has none), checked as a create's.

metadata.description: Labels added to the source's (a key here replaces the source's), at most 31 keys here and 32 in all (`instabox-fork-of` is set to the source's ID). Absent: the source's labels.

name.description: The new sandbox's name (as in CreateMachineRequest). Absent: `<source>-fork-` and 4 random hex digits.

secrets.description: The fork's own proxy selection, as in CreateMachineRequest. Absent together with envSecrets and directSecrets: the source's selection is copied.

vcpus.description: With `memMiB`, one of the org's sizes, or of the template's `defaultSpec` and `sizes` when it has a `pool`. Absent: the source's size.

account.description: The GitHub user or organization login the App is installed on.

suspended.description: Suspended on GitHub; its jobs start no boxes.

actor.description: The GitHub login that triggered its run; left out for a job recorded before it was.

branch.description: Its run's head branch; left out for a job recorded before it was.

commit.description: Its run's head commit SHA; left out for a job recorded before it was.

completionSource.description: How instabox learned the job completed: webhook (GitHub's completed event), runner_gone (GitHub removed its runner and answered the job ended), runner_gone_timeout (GitHub removed its runner but still had the job running after instabox waited 5 minutes; the box was deleted anyway), github_api (GitHub's job API answered the job ended: a runner-pool job, or one whose completed event never came because its box is gone or GitHub refuses instabox its runner) or access_lost (GitHub refused instabox the job for 5 minutes, as after its repository is removed from the instabox GitHub App or the App is suspended or uninstalled; instabox ended it without GitHub's result and deleted its box). Left out before it completes and for jobs completed before it was recorded.

conclusion.description: GitHub's conclusion once completed: success, failure, cancelled...

machineId.description: The CI box the job holds: its own, or one handed to it while it waited. Omitted once it ran on another runner than that box's (ranOn).

ranOn.description: The runner GitHub ran the job on.

readyAt.description: When instabox first had a runner ready for the job (its CI box's runner registered and started, or the pool runner that ran it; never before createdAt). Splits the wait: box ready (instabox's) up to it, pickup (GitHub's) from it to startedAt. Left out when not known: a job recorded before it was, or one GitHub ran on another job's box before its own runner was ready.

reason.description: Why the job waits, was refused or failed.

snapshot.description: The snapshot (name or ID, lower-case) its `SIZE-snapshot-<snapshot>` label (e.g. `instabox-medium-snapshot-acme-warm`) starts its box from instead of the stock `ci` template: a ready snapshot of a `ci` machine in the org the App install is linked to, else the job is refused, as is one of a public repository or of one that runs workflows of pull requests from forks. Absent: none.

startedAt.description: When a runner took it; the wait is from createdAt.

GitHubJobCounts.description: The org's jobs in each state group that `state` takes.

failed.description: Ran to its end on a CI box with conclusion `failure` or `timed_out`.

other.description: Did not run (refused, failed to start, cancelled first), ended otherwise (`cancelled`, `skipped`) or not done yet.

boxCreatedAt.description: When its own CI box was created. Absent: no box yet, or GitHub ran the job on another job's box.

commit.description: Its run's commit SHA, from GitHub.

failedStep.description: The first step that failed, from GitHub.

hasMore.description: More jobs of the state group asked for follow this page (next: offset + limit).

installUrl.description: Where an owner or admin installs the App and links it to the org, in a browser signed in to instabox.

linked.description: An install of the GitHub App is linked to the org.

unlinked.description: Installs unlinked from the org when the member who linked them left it; their jobs start nothing until an owner or admin links them again.

GitHubJobRun.description: Seconds from a runner taking the job to its end. Absent when no job ended.

GitHubJobSetup.description: What the CI page's setup steps count: only the jobs of the installs linked to the org now. An App uninstalled and installed again is a new install, so the setup starts over while the old jobs stay listed and in `counts`.

ran.description: A job ran to its end on a CI box, whatever its conclusion.

buckets.description: With step: every step from from, oldest first.

bySize.description: Each size with jobs, small to large.

ran.description: Jobs that ran to their end on a CI box, whatever their conclusion.

step.description: The step asked for, in seconds.

GitHubJobWait.description: Seconds from queued to a runner taking the job. Absent when no job was taken.

handover.description: Median until GitHub gave the box's runner the job.

pickup.description: Pickup: from a runner ready to the runner taking the job (GitHub's part), over the same jobs.

ready.description: Box ready: from queued to a runner ready for the job (instabox's part), over the jobs with a readyAt.

slot.description: Median until the CI box was created (plan limits, capacity), over jobs that ran on their own box.

GitHubJobWaitPart.description: A part of the wait in seconds. Absent when no job of the range has a readyAt.

p50.description: Seconds; absent when none of its jobs was taken.

account.description: The GitHub user or organization login the App is installed on.

reason.description: Why it was unlinked, e.g. `unlinked when alice left the workspace`.

publicKey.description: SSH host certificate authority's public key, in authorized_keys format.

values.description: Names and values to replace atomically; omitted names stay unchanged. Null values are rejected.

LegacyVaultExport.description: Explicit original-owner recovery of a retained legacy item. Save privately; contains a real value.

abuseLock.description: With cooldownReason: what the owner is told about the pause behind the lock. Absent when cooldownReason is.

archiveAt.description: When the sandbox is stopped if it is running (set at creation with `archiveSeconds`): its files are kept and a start brings it back. Resuming does not clear it; a sandbox that is not running when it passes only has it cleared. Absent: none.

autoSuspendAfterSeconds.description: The running sandbox is paused once it has been idle this many seconds (no agent working, no terminal input or output, little CPU); null: off. Pause, resume, stop and start keep it.

autoSuspendedAt.description: When the sandbox was queued to pause automatically; a successful automatic resume or its next explicit operation clears it. Absent: none.

cooldownReason.description: While cooldownUntil has not passed, the automatic abuse check whose pause locks the sandbox, the same as a wake's 409 `machine_cooldown` Error.reason: `abuse_egress_blocklist` (it tried to connect to a blocked destination on the egress blocklist, not a DNS lookup), `abuse_network_flows` (scanning or attack traffic), `abuse_cpu` (mining). Absent for a max-run cooldown, and once the lock ends.

cooldownUntil.description: All wake paths are refused until this deadline, including admin actions: after a max-run suspension, or the 24-hour lock of an automatic abuse check's pause (cooldownReason).

deleteAt.description: When the sandbox is deleted, whatever its state (set at creation with `deleteAfterSeconds`). The delete is an ordinary `delete` operation (`trigger: delete_at`), queued at `deleteAt` (within about a second) once no other operation is in progress. Absent: never.

earlyAllowanceEnded.description: Set on a stopped or paused free sandbox that cannot be started because its org's early free-sandbox allowance ended and as many free sandboxes as the standard limit allows are running: a start is refused (`402 early_allowance_ended`) until one is paused or deleted. Absent otherwise.

envNames.description: The names of the sandbox's create-time `env`, sorted. Absent when it has none. The values are never shown: read them in the sandbox.

free.description: A free-tier org's sandbox (docs/pricing.md): never billed, pauses after 30 idle minutes (another `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` is refused with 403). On a paid plan every sandbox is billed.

guestUser.description: The Linux user in the sandbox that SSH sessions, exec and the terminal log in as, fixed at create: the `guestUser` the create named, else `user` (a create from a snapshot: the snapshot's user). `dev` on sandboxes from templates without the `guest-user` capability, and on every sandbox created before the field.

image.description: Deprecated: `snapshot`, under its old name (same value).

lastOom.description: The newest OOM kill (absent until one is seen, or when the kernel log no longer held it).

oomKills.description: Processes the sandbox's kernel OOM killer killed since the sandbox was created (out of memory, or a memory cgroup's limit). Read from the sandbox about once a minute while it runs, and after an exec that exits non-zero; 0 on sandboxes whose host or guest agent predates the reading (absent from older servers).

orgId.description: The org the sandbox counts against (docs/orgs.md).

readyAt.description: When the running sandbox last became ready (`runtime.ready` turned true: SSH, exec and files work). For a new sandbox, `readyAt` minus `createdAt` is its create time; after a start or resume it is that start's. Absent while the sandbox is not ready, and on a sandbox that was already ready before the field existed (until its next start or resume).

runStartedAt.description: Start of the current continuous run, conservatively initialized on a first error observation too; resets only after confirmed sleep.

suspendable.description: false: the sandbox cannot be paused, since its hosts keep no memory of a running sandbox (macOS). Stop the sandbox instead; its files are kept. Absent: it can.

vault.description: Whether legacy Vault delivery is enabled. Independent of org Secret selections and delivery status at the sandbox's /secrets endpoint.

MachineAbuseLock.description: The owner's account of the abuse check's pause behind a sandbox's cooldownReason: when, what the sandbox did in a sentence (explanation) and in detail (what, with the exact address of a blocked destination, the address and port of a brute force, the swept port or scanned host and the count of a scan, the CPU share and, when the check confirmed it, the mining program and its pool), and how to appeal.

coreShare.description: The CPU check's mean share of the sandbox's vCPUs.

count.description: A network-flows finding's destinations, ports or connections.

dst.description: The blocked destination, the brute-forced or scanned address.

explanation.description: One plain sentence on what the sandbox did ("was reaching known abuse addresses ...").

kind.description: A network-flows finding's kind: sweep, scan, brute or fanout.

port.description: A brute force's destination port, or the swept port. A blocked destination's port is not recorded (the node keeps the address alone).

process.description: The mining program the CPU check found running, when it confirmed one.

what.description: The finding with its exact address and counts ("connected to blocked 47.91.89.3", "30 connections to 198.51.100.7:22 (brute force)", "swept port 22 across 500 destinations").

filesystems.description: `/data`, then `/` (`/` alone where `/data` is not a filesystem of its own).

warning.description: Set when a filesystem is at least 90% full (bytes or inodes).

availableBytes.description: What the sandbox's user can still write.

level.description: `ok` below 80%, `high` from 80%, `critical` from 90%, `full` at 100% (bytes or inodes).

usedPct.description: Used over used + available, 0-100 (df's Use%): writes fail with ENOSPC at 100.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

console.description: Console output: the last `tail` lines, or with `after`, the output written since that cursor. Empty when there is none or with `consoleUnavailable`.

consoleReset.description: `after` was past the end of the log because it was rotated and the kept previous 8 MiB no longer reach back to the cursor, so `console` starts again at the beginning of the current log and output in between is missing. A rotation the kept copy covers carries on without it. Absent when false.

consoleTruncated.description: There is older console output than `console`: the log goes back further than `tail` lines, or than the bytes read for them (256 per line, at least 64 KiB, at most 1 MiB), so long lines give fewer than `tail`. Absent when false and with `after`.

consoleUnavailable.description: Why there is no console output, e.g. the sandbox's disks are in storage or its host is not answering. Absent when the console was read.

cursor.description: Where `console` ends; pass it as `after` to read only newer output.

state.description: The sandbox's state, as on Machine.

MachineMetric.description: One sample, measured on the host. Bytes throughout.

cpuUsedPct.description: CPU time used over the sandbox's vCPUs, 0-100.

diskReadBytesPerSec.description: Storage reads, bytes per second over 90 s. Absent where the host does not report them yet.

diskTotal.description: Disk (`/data`) size; the root filesystem is not counted.

diskUsed.description: `/data`'s used bytes, on the latest sample of a running sandbox only (read inside it: the last read, refreshed in the background at most once a minute and at most 10 minutes old); absent otherwise. `disk` on the response has both filesystems.

diskWriteBytesPerSec.description: Storage writes, bytes per second over 90 s. Absent where the host does not report them yet.

gpuCount.description: GPU sandboxes only: the sandbox's GPUs.

gpuMemTotal.description: GPU sandboxes only: its GPU type's memory times gpuCount, bytes.

gpuMemUsed.description: GPU sandboxes only: GPU memory in use, bytes, summed over the sandbox's GPUs. Absent where the host did not read it.

gpuUsedPct.description: GPU sandboxes only: the share of the time a kernel ran on the sandbox's GPUs, averaged over them (0-100). Absent where the host did not read it.

memUsed.description: Guest memory touched (it drops only when memory is reclaimed).

netInBytesPerSec.description: Network traffic to the sandbox, bytes per second over 90 s. Leaves out SSH and public port traffic. Absent where the host does not report it yet.

netOutBytesPerSec.description: Network traffic from the sandbox (egress), bytes per second over 90 s. Leaves out SSH and public port traffic. Absent where the host does not report it yet.

disk.description: The running sandbox's filesystem use, read inside it (the last read, refreshed in the background at most once a minute and at most 10 minutes old; the route never reads it itself, so the first call after a while may not have it); absent while it is not running or not read yet.

directSecrets.description: Direct references (names and paths, never values), envSecrets included.

envSecrets.description: Direct references that are exactly the same-name shorthand ({secret X, env X}, no file). Renamed and file references appear only in directSecrets.

items.description: Effective selected Secrets, including proxy all. Metadata only.

usage.description: Present when the server records proxied request counts: one entry per selected proxy Secret.

version.description: Version of this sandbox's selection configuration.

gpuType.description: The GPU type of its GPUs (`GET /v1/templates` `gpuTypes`); absent on a sandbox without one.

gpus.description: GPUs of `gpuType` the sandbox has (`gpu` on create); absent on a sandbox without one.

rootDiskGiB.description: System disk size in GiB, set by the template (only admins change it); absent: the template's.

diskGiBSeconds.description: Disk (`/data`) size, current size, times the seconds the sandbox existed in the window.

egressBytes.description: Bytes the sandbox sent to the public internet, by whole hour: every hour from the one `from` falls in up to `to`. Billed or not (the plan's free egress and free sandboxes included).

runningSeconds.description: Seconds the sandbox was running in the window.

applied.description: The last write into the machine; null: none yet.

items.description: The items that apply with the machine's current metadata (none when enabled is false).

MaxRunMinutes.description: Maximum continuous runtime in minutes. -1 is unlimited; 0 sleeps immediately. Independent of idle auto-pause; whichever condition is reached first pauses the sandbox. Free machines default to 480 and only an admin session can change them. The service manages free runtime and may pause a run earlier. The response reports the current limit from runStartedAt; it can change during the run. Paid machines default to -1 and their users can change this setting. Max-run suspension starts a cooldown, returning 409 machine_cooldown with Retry-After on every wake path. By default it is 5 to 20 minutes (5 plus a random 0 to 15) on a paid plan and for the first such pause in a row on the free plan. Back-to-back pauses on the free plan rest longer (60 to 75, then 120 to 135 minutes): "Longer cooldowns on the free plan" at https://instabox.sh/docs/machines/auto-pause#longer-cooldowns-on-the-free-plan. Once cooldown ends, 0 still refuses wake with 409 max_run_disabled until changed.

activated.description: This account passed the invite gate (admins always have). When `inviteRequired` and not `activated`, every route but this one, `POST /v1/invites/redeem` and `POST /v1/auth/logout` answers `403 invite_required`.

admin.description: The user is an admin and may use the admin-only endpoints (`/v1/admin`).

adminUrl.description: Admins only: the origin of the admin console when it has its own (the server's `adminUrl`). Absent, the console is `/admin/` on the dashboard's origin.

allowedSpecs.description: The sizes your new sandboxes may have in your personal org (no `rootDiskGiB`: the template's). The first is the server's `limits.machineSpec` (4 vCPUs and 8 GiB memory by default), what a create naming no size gets; the others are your plan's (Pro: 2/4, 4/8, 8/16; Builder: 2/4 up to 16/32; Team and Enterprise: 2/4 up to 32/64) and sizes an admin granted you, picked by naming their `vcpus` and `memMiB` on create. Any other size is refused with `spec_not_allowed`, admins included.

alwaysOnAllowed.description: Whether 0 (off) is a choice too, on `org`'s plan (the personal org's for a sign-in session). A sandbox in another org follows that org's plan: see its `workspaces` entry's `alwaysOnAllowed`.

billingEnabled.description: Paid plans can be subscribed: the server has Stripe configured. False: the dashboard offers no plan actions and the billing routes answer 503.

csrfToken.description: Browser sessions only. Send it as `X-Instabox-CSRF` on every request that is not GET or HEAD.

directSecretRefs.description: This site takes direct Secret file references and renamed variables (`directSecrets`) and exec `secretEnvs`. Absent: they are refused with 400 (same-name references work); clients should not send them, since a control host from before them would ignore or misread them.

diskResize.description: An admin's override of disk growth (`PATCH /v1/machines/{id}` `persistentDiskGiB`, `rootDiskGiB`): `allow` grows free sandboxes' disks too, `deny` none. Absent: paid sandboxes grow, free ones are fixed.

email.description: The account's email, which an org invite must be sent to for it to join.

emailInvites.description: This server emails workspace invites (server.json `email`). Absent: creating or resending an invite answers 503.

fixedAutoSuspendSeconds.description: The idle auto-suspend every sandbox of this account gets on a server that offers no choice; absent when the account chooses (`manualLifecycle`, or `idleChoicesSeconds`).

idleChoicesSeconds.description: The idle times offered (300 to 1800, 5 to 30 minutes; docs/pricing.md): a request may send any whole minute from the first to the last. 0 (off) is never listed: `alwaysOnAllowed` says whether it is a choice too. Absent with `manualLifecycle`.

inviteRequired.description: This server gates new accounts behind an invite code (docs/invites.md).

login.description: GitHub login at last sign-in (display only).

machineMetrics.description: Clients show this account per-sandbox metrics (the dashboard's Metrics tab, `instabox metrics`): admins always, every account once the server sets `machineMetricsForAll`. Absent: hidden. `GET /v1/machines/{id}/metrics` answers either way.

manualLifecycle.description: An admin let this account manage its sandboxes' lifecycle (docs/idle-suspend.md): the `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` it sends applies (0: off). Otherwise every sandbox pauses after `fixedAutoSuspendSeconds` idle, whatever a request says.

org.description: The org `allowedSpecs`, `idleChoicesSeconds` and `alwaysOnAllowed` describe: your personal org, or a workspace key's workspace. Absent from older servers.

orgId.description: Set for a workspace API key: its workspace. The user is then the workspace's owner, whom the key acts as.

paidActivation.description: An account the invite gate holds back may buy a workspace (`POST /v1/orgs`) instead, and is activated once its plan takes effect (docs/invites.md). Absent: only an invite code lets it in.

plans.description: The paid plans an org can go on (Pro, Builder, Team) as this server sells them, for plan pickers.

resizeRestart.description: This server takes `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}` `apply: "restart"` (one stop, resize, start operation). Absent: it answers `400 resize_restart_off`; resize with your own stop, `PATCH`, start.

termsVersion.description: The version of the rules of the road (the Terms of Service's acceptable use) this account last agreed to (`PUT /v1/me/terms`). Absent: none.

waitlist.description: The account's place in the line invite codes go out from and its referral link (docs/invites.md, "Referrals"). Absent: not in line (activated, the gate off, or a live code claimed for its email).

position.description: Absent when this server could not rank the line just now.

webhooksEnabled.description: This server offers org webhooks (docs/webhooks.md). False: the dashboard hides them, the CLI says they are off and the webhook routes answer 404.

workspaces.description: Your other orgs, each with its own plan and limits (`GET /v1/usage?org=ID`, `GET /v1/orgs/{id}`). Omitted when there are none, and for a workspace API key, which reaches only its own org.

Metadata.description: String labels. At most 32 keys of 1-64 characters `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, values of at most 512 characters, 8 KiB as JSON.

oomKill.description: The newest OOM kill whose victim was in the cgroup (absent: none named).

bootId.description: The sandbox boot the job ran in (/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id): only that boot's kills are returned, since session scope names repeat after a restart.

cgroup.description: A background job's cgroup in the sandbox: a session scope such as /user.slice/user-1000.slice/session-3.scope.

OOMKill.description: A process the sandbox's kernel OOM killer killed.

at.description: When it was killed (to about a second).

cgroup.description: A memory cgroup's limit killed it (a container, a unit's MemoryMax), not the sandbox running out of memory.

process.description: The killed process's name: its comm (at most 15 bytes from the kernel), capped at 64 bytes.

rssBytes.description: Its resident memory when it was killed (anonymous, file and shared).

uid.description: The killed process's user ID, when the kernel logged it.

Operation.description: The progress of a change to a sandbox (`suspend` is pause; `restore` puts its disks back to a snapshot's; `move`, admin only, copies it to another host pool). It does not return the request it was queued with (a start's `vcpus`/`memMiB` show in the sandbox's `spec`).

forkInherited.description: On the answer to `POST /v1/machines/{id}/fork`: the control host that took it keeps the source's delete deadline, idle auto-suspend, max run and metadata, and takes `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` and `maxRunMinutes`. Absent: a host from before that (during a rolling control deploy), which gave the fork its defaults with only the request's `metadata` and `deleteAfterSeconds`; set the idle auto-suspend and max run with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`.

machine.description: The sandbox as it is when `GET /v1/operations/{id}` is read. Included when the operation `succeeded`, the sandbox still exists, and the caller may read sandboxes (`machines:read` for API keys). Later operations can change it; it is not a record of the state at completion. Absent otherwise, and from older servers.

phase.description: Free text progress, e.g. scheduling, booting, waiting_ready, snapshotting.

trigger.description: Set when instabox started the operation itself: `idle` (paused when idle), `max_run` (maximum continuous runtime), `memory_pressure` (paused, its processes kept, because the host it ran on was running out of memory; the next use wakes it, as after `idle`), `request` (wake on use), `wake` (POST /v1/machines/{id}/wake), `timeout`, `archive`, `delete_at` (the sandbox's `deleteAt` passed), `drain` (maintenance by an admin), `user_delete` (an admin deleted the owner), `user_disable` (an admin disabled the owner), `admin` (an admin stopped or paused the sandbox), `admin_delete` (an admin deleted the sandbox), `credit` (its free-tier org used up the month's included usage), `spend_cap`, `downgrade`, `subscription_ended`, `payment_method` (its free workspace has no card on file), `members` (its free workspace has more members than the free plan allows), `early_allowance_ended` (paused because the account's early free-sandbox allowance ended and it has more free sandboxes than the free plan runs), `abuse_pool` (paused because the sandbox tried to connect to a blocked destination on the egress blocklist, such as a crypto-mining pool; a DNS lookup of a listed domain never suspends) or `abuse_cpu` (paused by the CPU abuse detector: a restricted account's sandbox ran flat out for an hour with no memory use, no public port, nobody using it and a connection to a mining port) or `abuse_scan` (paused by the flow detector: a restricted account's sandbox swept one port across many hosts, scanned many ports of one host or brute-forced a login port). Absent: a client request.

serverPublicKey.description: The runtime's NaCl box public key (base64).

issuer.description: The `iss` of assertions (the server's public URL).

Org.description: An org (docs/orgs.md). Sandboxes are created in one and count against its plan.

allowedSpecs.description: The sizes that may be created in the org, the default first (its plan's, then any an admin granted the org).

cardMissingAt.description: Set while a workspace has no card on file. On the free tier its sandboxes then answer `402 payment_method_required` and running ones are paused (`trigger: payment_method`); they run again once one is added (`POST /v1/orgs/{id}/billing/checkout` with no tier, or the portal).

disabledAt.description: Set while the workspace cannot be used: its plan ended (cancelled, unpaid, or its credits ran out). Its sandboxes answer `402 subscription_required`; they and its snapshots are deleted 30 days later unless it subscribes again.

kind.description: `personal`: the account's own org, made when it signed up, on any tier but with no other members: it takes no invites. `workspace`: an org to share, on any tier; on the free tier it needs a card on file and has up to `limits.maxMembers` members.

purgeAt.description: Set on a disabled workspace: when its sandboxes and snapshots are deleted. Until then its people can download their `/data` (`POST /v1/orgs/{id}/exports`).

OrgBilling.description: The org's Stripe subscription (docs/pricing.md); absent when it never had one.

funding.description: What pays the plan: a Stripe subscription, or the org's credits (renewed by the server on the 1st).

graceUntil.description: When an unpaid subscription ends (the failed charge's time; the next billing pass ends it).

scheduledTier.description: A lower tier that applies at the next renewal.

status.description: `incomplete`: Checkout not completed; `past_due`: a charge failed, the plan stays until the next billing pass ends it (`graceUntil`).

unpaidInvoiceIds.description: Stripe invoices whose charge failed and are still open; until they are paid (the billing portal) the org cannot subscribe again, and a subscription it completed meanwhile does not take effect.

OrgGPUUsage.description: One GPU type's usage this month (`OrgUsage.gpu`).

hourUSD.description: The current price per GPU-hour (0: not priced).

email.description: Where the invite was emailed, lowercased. Absent: a code with no recipient.

maxUses.description: How many people the workspace's codes let in together.

redeemers.description: Who joined with any of the workspace's codes and when, oldest first.

state.description: `used`: nobody else can join with it.

useCount.description: How many people joined with any of the workspace's codes.

email.description: The account's provider-verified email. Absent: it has none.

alwaysOn.description: Whether the plan's sandboxes may turn idle auto-suspend off.

earlyAllowanceEnded.description: True when the org's early free-sandbox allowance (five, until 2026-12-01 00:00 UTC) has ended and it has more free sandboxes than `freeSandboxes`: only that many may run, the others are paused and a start of one is refused (`402 early_allowance_ended`). Absent otherwise.

freeSandboxHours.description: The free sandboxes' running time a month when the server caps it; 0: no cap.

freeSandboxes.description: The free tier's sandbox allowance (never billed): limits.maxMachinesPerUser, or an admin's override on the org.

maxDiskGiB.description: How far its owner may grow a sandbox's disk (`/data`), in GiB (free 20, fixed: it neither grows nor shrinks; pro 200; builder 500; team and enterprise 1024); a disk already past it is kept. 0: no limit.

maxMachines.description: Sandboxes the org may have, in any state: on the free tier its allowance (`freeSandboxes`, never billed), on a paid plan the plan's count, every one billed; 0: no limit. An org over it keeps what it has but creates nothing more.

maxMembers.description: Members the org may have, its owner and pending invites included; 0: no limit (a personal org: 1).

maxRunning.description: Paid sandboxes that may run at once; 0: no limit.

maxSnapshots.description: Live snapshots the org may have; 0: no limit.

maxStoredGiB.description: Cap on the disk (`/data`) allocated to the org's live sandboxes, in GiB: new sandboxes and snapshots in the org are refused (`429 quota_exceeded`) while it is over. 0: no limit.

maxVCPUs.description: The largest sandbox size the plan offers, by vCPUs.

monthlyCreditUSD.description: Always 0 (kept for older clients); the free sandbox has hours, not a credit.

overageAlert.description: Whether a paid org's owner and admins are emailed once a month when usage goes beyond what the month includes (pay as you go).

spendCapUSD.description: A paid org's cap on this month's usage beyond its allowance (`PATCH /v1/orgs/{id}/billing`); null when none, 0 when nothing beyond the allowance is allowed.

startsPerMinute.description: Sandbox starts (create, start, resume, wake) the org may make a minute; 0: no limit.

thresholdBillingUSD.description: Usage beyond what the month includes is charged to the card each time what is not charged yet reaches this, rather than all at the month's end; absent when only at the end, and for an org that is not charged so (credits-funded, no subscription, or a plan without a monthly fee).

usageAlertPercent.description: A paid org's usage alert: its owner and admins are emailed once a month when usage reaches this share of what the month includes (the allowance plus the credits); 0: off. Absent where no email would go out: the free tier, billing off, no active or past-due subscription, or a plan without a monthly fee (enterprise) and no credits.

computeUSD.description: vCPU and memory at list prices, before the plan's allowance; 0 for a free sandbox.

deletedAt.description: When the sandbox was deleted; absent for a live one.

free.description: A free sandbox; its compute is not billed.

gpuSeconds.description: GPUs times running seconds in the window; absent without GPUs.

gpuType.description: Their GPU type; absent without one.

gpuUSD.description: Its GPU time at the type's price per GPU-hour; absent without GPUs.

gpus.description: The sandbox's GPUs; absent without one.

runningSeconds.description: Seconds the sandbox was running in the window.

total.description: Sandboxes in the list, all pages.

alwaysOnAllowed.description: Set on `GET /v1/me` (`org`, `workspaces`): this org's plan lets its sandboxes take `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` 0 (off). Absent on a plan that does not, elsewhere, and from older servers.

OrgUsage.description: The org's usage this calendar month (UTC) as the hourly rating job priced it: running time by sandbox size, the allocated disk (`/data`) of the paid sandboxes beyond the plan's included disk, and egress beyond the plan's free egress a month, up to `ratedUntil`. Snapshots and the system disk are not billed.

allocatedDiskGiB.description: The `/data` of all the org's live sandboxes, free ones included, in GiB: what `limits.maxStoredGiB` is checked against.

allowanceUSD.description: Usage the month includes: the free credit, or what the subscription paid for.

billableDiskGiB.description: The disk being billed now: the sum over the org's paid sandboxes of their allocated `/data` (less `freeDiskGiBPerSandbox` each, 0 by default), less `includedDiskGiB`; 0 while the org is past due or disabled (nothing is rated then), and without sandboxes of an earlier account life.

chargedUSD.description: Usage beyond the allowance already charged this month (threshold billing); the month's end bills overageUSD less it.

costUSD.description: This month's usage so far, at the prices in force when rated.

creditsExpireAt.description: When the earliest of the credits expires.

creditsUSD.description: What the org's unexpired credits have left: they pay a plan's fee and usage beyond the allowance (docs/pricing.md, Credits).

egressGiB.description: Egress to the public internet beyond the plan's free egress this month (metered per machine, rated hourly).

freeDiskGiBPerSandbox.description: The `/data` of each paid sandbox that is not billed, in GiB: 0 by default (every allocated GiB is billed); an operator may configure more. Absent from older servers, which did not bill the first 20 GiB.

freeMachines.description: Of them, the free sandboxes (never billed).

freeSandboxHours.description: The free sandboxes' running time this month.

gpu.description: This month's GPU time by GPU type, rated per GPU-hour while the sandboxes run (in costUSD). Absent while the org has no GPU usage this month.

gpuUSD.description: The sum of `gpu`'s `usd`: the GPU part of costUSD.

includedDiskGiB.description: The disk the org's plan includes, all its paid sandboxes' `/data` together, in GiB (Pro 200, Builder 1024, Team and Enterprise 5120): each hour that much is not billed. Absent from older servers, which included none.

overageUSD.description: Usage beyond the allowance (billed at month end on a paid tier).

remainingUSD.description: What may still be used before the org is stopped; 0 when there is no limit or nothing is left (see `limits`).

running.description: The paid sandboxes running or starting now: what `limits.maxRunning` is checked against when a sandbox is created, started or resumed.

storageGiBHours.description: Allocated disk (`/data`) of the paid sandboxes (less `freeDiskGiBPerSandbox` each, 0 by default) beyond the plan's `includedDiskGiB` each hour, in GiB-hours.

storedBytes.description: Deprecated: always null. Storage is billed on allocated disk, not stored bytes; use `billableDiskGiB`.

PlanOffer.description: A paid plan as this server sells it (server.json `plans`).

maxDiskGiB.description: How far a sandbox's disk (`/data`) may grow on this plan, in GiB (free 20, fixed: it neither grows nor shrinks; pro 200; builder 500; team and enterprise 1024); a disk already past it is kept. 0: no limit.

maxMachines.description: Sandboxes the org may have on this plan, every one billed; 0: no limit.

maxRunning.description: Paid sandboxes running at once; 0: no limit.

monthlyFeeUSD.description: The monthly fee, also the usage it includes each month.

url.description: The Stripe customer portal URL to send the user to.

live.description: The list was read from the running sandbox for this request; false: the list the server stored last, for a stopped or paused sandbox.

processes.description: Without `all`, kernel threads and the listing's own processes are left out.

trigger.description: What read it: a client's request, or the server just before a stop or a pause.

truncated.description: The listing was cut; processes are missing.

access.description: `public`: anyone with the URL. `private`: only requests that carry the port's token (`_token` query parameter once, the cookie it sets, or `Authorization: Bearer`).

address.description: `tcp` only: the TLS endpoint `host:port`; the client must send the host as SNI. psql: `host=<host> port=<port> sslmode=require`.

expiresAt.description: Always null (public ports do not expire); kept for older in-guest instabox-port agents.

id.description: The publication's ID; a new one after an unpublish, an access change or a token rotation. The URL does not change.

protocol.description: `http`: an HTTPS URL. `tcp`: a raw TCP service behind TLS at `address`, routed by SNI, always public (docs/public-ports.md, "Raw TCP ports").

token.description: A private port's token (`ibp_...`), only in the publish response that created or rotated it.

tokenUrl.description: `url` with `?_token=<token>`: the link to share. Present with `token`.

url.description: `https://<port>-<sandbox>.<domain>` for `http`, `tls://<address>` for `tcp`. Empty when public ports (or raw TCP ports) are not configured.

enabled.description: Whether the server has public ports configured.

access.description: Omitted: the current access, or public for a new port. Changing it ends the old publication's connections. `private` is for `http` ports only.

name.description: Omitted: the current name, or "Port N" for a new port.

port.description: Desktop port 5901 and Orca port 6768 (plus the configured Orca port) are reserved.

protocol.description: Omitted: the current protocol, or `http` for a new port. `tcp` publishes a raw TCP service behind TLS when the server enables it (403 otherwise; admins only while in preview); paid plans only, at most 5 per org by default (429). A port already published with the other protocol answers 409 until it is unpublished. A `tcp` port cannot be private (400).

rotateToken.description: With a private port: a new token, returned in the response; connections that used the old one close. 400 for a public port.

path.description: File items only: the target, relative to the home directory.

selector.description: Absent or {}: the item applies to every machine.

value.description: UTF-8 text without NUL bytes, 1 byte to 64 KiB, stored as given.

code.description: An invite code (`K7R2QX`; older `482913` and `ibi_...` codes work too); spaces around it, spaces or dashes inside a 6-character code (`K7R 2QX`) and case do not matter.

desiredState.description: `running` (default) boots the restored disks; `stopped` leaves the sandbox stopped with them.

snapshotId.description: The snapshot whose disks the sandbox gets (`sn_...`, or an older `im_...` ID). Absent: the snapshot the sandbox was created from; a sandbox created from a template needs it (`400`).

timeoutSeconds.description: For a running sandbox: how long to wait for a clean shutdown before it is forced off (0-600; 0: the server default), as for stop.

ResumeMachineRequest.description: A body key that is none of these is refused with `400 unknown_field` (keys match case-insensitively); an empty body or `{}` is valid.

vault.description: False disables legacy Vault delivery without changing org Secret selections.

processesPreserved.description: Set after a start or resume. False means the paused programs could not be brought back and the sandbox booted fresh (files are kept).

ready.description: True only when the sandbox is running, reports all checks passing and, as checked when it boots or resumes, accepts exec, file and SSH connections.

expiresAt.description: Absent: the token does not expire (`noExpiry`).

hostKeyFingerprint.description: SHA256 fingerprint of the SSH server's host key, which ssh asks to confirm on the first connection.

id.description: Connection ID (`cn_…`) of the token's grant.

moshCommand.description: The same login with mosh: `mosh --ssh="ssh -p <port>" <token>@<host>` (`mosh <token>@<host>` on port 22). Absent when mosh is not available.

token.description: `ibssh_` and 26 lowercase base32 characters (128 bits): the SSH user name. Shown only here.

expiresAt.description: Absent: the token does not expire.

host.description: With `port`, `token`, `command` and `moshCommand`: set only in a sign-in session, for a valid token the caller made, when the server kept it (a vault key is configured).

Secret.description: Org Secret metadata. Values, ciphertext and placeholders are never returned.

id.description: Stable identity retained by replacements; deletion and recreation makes a new ID.

SecretDelivery.description: Proxy supplies an opaque sandbox-specific placeholder for substitution in ordinary HTTPS headers on allowed hosts (port 443). Env supplies the real value, including credentials needed by native database clients. Unsupported traffic never falls back from proxy to env.

file.description: A direct Secret's home-relative file path.

SecretGuestStatus.description: Managed environment and public CA installation. This does not prove existing processes reloaded values. Removing env access cannot remove values already copied into process memory, files, or snapshots.

appliedRevision.description: Revision of the last installation attempt; check state for success.

error.description: Fixed delivery error, never arbitrary guest output or credential values.

items.description: Metadata from the last successful installation.

SecretHosts.description: Exact ASCII DNS hostnames, normalized to lowercase without a trailing dot, or a standalone `*` for every public HTTPS destination.
